questions.concept: Four basic functions of a computer
questions.question: According to William Stallings' top-level functional view, what are the four main functions that a computer performs?
options: Data processing, data storage, data movement, and control
Input, compilation, virtualization, and networking
Fetching, pipelining, branch prediction, and caching
Arithmetic calculation, bus arbitration, paging, and interrupt handling
questions.explanationEn: A computer performs four fundamental functions: Data Processing, Data Storage (short-term and long-term), Data Movement (I/O with peripherals or data communications), and Control (managing resources and coordinating functional components).
questions.explanationVi: Máy tính thực hiện 4 chức năng cơ bản: Xử lý dữ liệu (Data Processing), Lưu trữ dữ liệu (Data Storage), Di chuyển dữ liệu (Data Movement / I/O), và Điều khiển (Control).

questions.subtopic: Computer Classes (PC, PMD, IoT, Server, WSC/Supercomputer)
questions.concept: Warehouse-Scale Computers and Supercomputers
questions.question: Which class of computers is characterized as a type of Warehouse-Scale Computer (WSC) or cluster specifically designed for high-performance scientific and engineering computation, typically costing from millions to hundreds of millions of USD?
options: Personal Mobile Devices (PMDs)
Embedded IoT Controllers
Supercomputers
Mid-range Enterprise Workstations
questions.explanationEn: Supercomputers are a specialized form of large-scale / Warehouse-Scale Computers (clusters) built for high-performance scientific and engineering computations, costing millions to hundreds of millions of USD.
questions.explanationVi: Siêu máy tính (Supercomputers) là một dạng máy tính quy mô kho (WSC/cluster) dùng cho tính toán khoa học và kỹ thuật hiệu năng cao, có chi phí từ hàng triệu đến hàng trăm triệu USD.

questions.concept: Data movement vs I/O
questions.question: When a computer receives sensor measurements from a device that is directly connected to the computer's local interface ports, what is this specific data movement process called?
options: Input/Output (I/O) involving peripheral devices
Teleprocessing over a wide-area network
Microprogrammed control sequencing
Instruction-level speculative execution
questions.explanationEn: When data is received from or sent to a device directly connected to the computer, the data movement process is called Input/Output (I/O), and the connected devices are referred to as peripherals.
questions.explanationVi: Khi dữ liệu được nhận từ hoặc gửi tới một thiết bị kết nối trực tiếp với máy tính, quá trình di chuyển dữ liệu này được gọi là vào/ra (Input/Output - I/O) thông qua các thiết bị ngoại vi (peripheral devices).

questions.concept: Computer Architecture vs. Computer Organization
questions.question: Which of the following attributes belongs to Computer Architecture rather than Computer Organization?
options: The physical circuit design of the adder inside the ALU
The hardware control signals used to refresh dynamic RAM cells
The specific semiconductor memory technology (SRAM vs. DRAM) used on the motherboard
The memory addressing modes and instruction formats visible to an assembly programmer
questions.explanationEn: Computer Architecture refers to the logical aspects of a system visible to the programmer (instruction set, instruction formats, data types, addressing modes), whereas Computer Organization covers the physical implementation details (circuit design, control signals, memory technology).
questions.explanationVi: Kiến trúc máy tính (Computer Architecture) bao gồm các khía cạnh logic nhìn từ góc độ người lập trình (tập lệnh, định dạng lệnh, kiểu dữ liệu, chế độ địa chỉ), còn Tổ chức máy tính (Computer Organization) bao gồm các khía cạnh vật lý (thiết kế mạch, tín hiệu điều khiển, công nghệ bộ nhớ).

questions.concept: Three fundamental components of Computer Architecture
questions.question: In the broader definition of Computer Architecture, what are its three fundamental components?
options: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), Microarchitecture, and System Design
Compiler, Assembler, and Linker
Control Unit, Arithmetic Logic Unit, and Input/Output Interface
Application Layer, Operating System Layer, and Digital Logic Layer
questions.explanationEn: Slides 1.9–1.11 define the three fundamental components of Computer Architecture as: (1) Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), (2) Microarchitecture (computer organization), and (3) System Design (buses, memory controllers, multiprocessing).
questions.explanationVi: Ba thành phần cơ bản của Kiến trúc máy tính là: Kiến trúc tập lệnh (ISA), Vi kiến trúc (Microarchitecture / tổ chức máy tính), và Thiết kế hệ thống (System Design).

questions.concept: Applying Architecture vs. Organization to processor families
questions.question: Intel's Core i5 and Core i7 processors from different generations can execute the exact same x86-64 machine code binaries, yet they differ in pipeline depth, cache sizes, and internal bus widths. How is this relationship best described?
options: They share the same Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) but have different Computer Organizations (Microarchitectures)
They share the same Computer Organization but have incompatible Instruction Set Architectures
They have identical Microarchitectures and System Designs but different High-Level Languages
They use Harvard architecture for user applications and Von Neumann architecture for system software
questions.explanationEn: Processors in the same family maintain backward binary compatibility by implementing the same Instruction Set Architecture (Architecture), while evolving their internal hardware implementation, pipeline, and cache hierarchy (Organization / Microarchitecture).
questions.explanationVi: Các bộ xử lý cùng họ duy trì tính tương thích mã máy bằng cách giữ nguyên Kiến trúc tập lệnh (ISA), nhưng thay đổi Tổ chức máy tính / Vi kiến trúc (độ sâu pipeline, dung lượng cache, mạch phần cứng).

questions.concept: ROM vs. RAM in Main Memory
questions.question: How does Read-Only Memory (ROM) differ from Random Access Memory (RAM) in a traditional computer's main memory?
options: ROM is non-volatile and retains system instructions when power is turned off, whereas RAM is volatile and loses its contents without power
ROM stores temporary user application data, whereas RAM permanently stores the BIOS firmware
ROM is accessed sequentially like magnetic tape, whereas RAM can only be written once at manufacture
ROM is located inside the ALU registers, whereas RAM is an external optical storage device
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.15 states that ROM stores system instructions/data and retains its contents even when power is turned off (non-volatile), whereas RAM stores system and user instructions/data and loses its contents when power is turned off (volatile).
questions.explanationVi: ROM lưu trữ lệnh/dữ liệu hệ thống và giữ nguyên nội dung khi tắt nguồn (bất khả biến), trong khi RAM lưu trữ lệnh/dữ liệu của hệ thống và người dùng nhưng bị mất dữ liệu khi tắt nguồn (khả biến).

questions.concept: Basic components inside a single core
questions.question: In a multicore processor chip (such as the 8-core architecture illustrated in Figure 1.2), which three basic functional logic blocks are contained inside each individual core alongside its L1/L2 caches?
options: Northbridge chipset, Southbridge I/O controller, and PCIe slot
Magnetic disk controller, DMA arbiter, and Ethernet transceiver
Instruction logic, Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU), and Load/store logic
Compiler, Assembler, and Virtual Memory Manager
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.33 specifies the basic components of a core: Instruction logic (fetching and decoding instructions), Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU, performing the specified operation), and Load/store logic (managing data transfer to/from main memory through cache).
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 1.33, các thành phần cơ bản bên trong một nhân (core) gồm: Instruction logic (nạp và giải mã lệnh), ALU (thực hiện phép toán số học/logic), và Load/store logic (quản lý truyền dữ liệu với bộ nhớ chính qua cache).

questions.concept: Cycle time from bus clock frequency
questions.question: A system bus operates at a clock frequency of 133 MHz. What is its clock cycle time in nanoseconds (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.explanationEn: Cycle time is the reciprocal of clock frequency: T = 1 / f = 1 / (133 * 10^6 cycles/sec) = 7.5188 * 10^-9 s ≈ 7.52 ns/cycle.
questions.explanationVi: Chu kỳ xung nhịp là nghịch đảo của tần số: T = 1 / f = 1 / (133 × 10^6 Hz) ≈ 7.52 ns.
questions.stepByStep:
1. Convert frequency to Hz: f = 133 MHz = 133 × 10^6 Hz.
2. Compute cycle period: T = 1 / (133 × 10^6) s = 7.51879 × 10^-9 s.
3. Convert seconds to nanoseconds (1 ns = 10^-9 s): T ≈ 7.52 ns.

questions.concept: Interpreting computer system advertisement specifications
questions.question: In the example desktop computer specification ('Intel Pentium Dual Core 3.06 GHz, 1333 MHz 4GB DDR SDRAM, 128KB L1 cache, 2MB L2 cache, 4 USB ports, 1 serial port, 1 parallel port, 4 PCI expansion slots'), how many total interface/expansion ports are listed on that system and how does a parallel port differ from a serial port?
options: 10 ports total; a parallel port sends data as a single pulse along at least 8 data lines simultaneously, whereas a serial port sends data as a series of pulses along 1 or 2 data lines
4 ports total; a parallel port sends data 1 bit at a time, whereas a serial port uses 64 data lines
8 ports total; a parallel port is self-configuring plug-and-play, whereas USB requires manual jumpers
12 ports total; both serial and parallel ports use optical fibers exclusively
questions.explanationEn: Slides 1.28–1.29 show the system has 10 ports in total (4 USB + 1 serial + 1 parallel + 4 PCI slots). Serial ports send data as a series of pulses along one or two data lines, whereas parallel ports send data as a single pulse along at least eight data lines.
questions.explanationVi: Hệ thống có tổng cộng 10 cổng (4 USB + 1 serial + 1 parallel + 4 khe PCI). Cổng nối tiếp (serial) truyền dữ liệu thành chuỗi xung trên 1 hoặc 2 đường dữ liệu, còn cổng song song (parallel) truyền đồng thời trên ít nhất 8 đường dữ liệu.

questions.concept: Binary vs Decimal metric prefixes
questions.question: When measuring main memory (RAM) capacity using binary powers of two versus measuring processor clock frequency using decimal powers of ten, what is the exact ratio between 1 Gigabyte (2^30 bytes) and 1 billion (10^9) cycles?
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.19 states that for storage, 1 GB = 2^30 = 1,073,741,824 Bytes, whereas for frequency/decimal metrics, Giga = 10^9 = 1,000,000,000.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 1.19, 1 GB bộ nhớ theo lũy thừa của 2 là 2^30 = 1,073,741,824 Bytes, trong khi tiền tố Giga theo hệ thập phân (xung nhịp) là 10^9 = 1,000,000,000.

questions.concept: The 7-level Computer Level Hierarchy
questions.question: In the 7-level Computer Level Hierarchy (Levels 0 through 6), which level lies immediately below Level 3 (System Software Level) and consists of instructions specific to the machine's architecture that require no compilers, interpreters, or assemblers?
options: Level 4: Assembly Language Level
Level 2: Machine Level (also known as the Instruction Set Architecture Level)
Level 1: Control Level (Microcode or Hardwired)
Level 0: Digital Logic Level (Gates and Wires)
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.36 and 1.38 show the hierarchy from top to bottom: Level 6 (User), Level 5 (High-Level Language), Level 4 (Assembly Language), Level 3 (System Software), Level 2 (Machine / ISA Level), Level 1 (Control), and Level 0 (Digital Logic).
questions.explanationVi: Thứ tự phân cấp từ cao xuống thấp: Level 6 (User), Level 5 (HLL), Level 4 (Assembly), Level 3 (System Software), Level 2 (Machine / ISA Level), Level 1 (Control), Level 0 (Digital Logic).

questions.concept: Level 1 Control Unit implementations
questions.question: At Level 1 (Control Level) of the Computer Level Hierarchy, what is the fundamental difference between a microprogrammed control unit and a hardwired control unit?
options: A microprogrammed control unit uses a low-level microprogram implemented by hardware to interpret instructions, whereas a hardwired control unit consists of digital hardware that directly executes machine instructions
A microprogrammed control unit only executes Java bytecode, whereas a hardwired control unit only executes Python scripts
A microprogrammed control unit is faster than a hardwired control unit and is exclusively used in RISC processors
A hardwired control unit requires an operating system kernel to decode each instruction
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.39 explains that at Level 1, control units can be microprogrammed (a program written in a low-level language implemented by hardware) or hardwired (hardware logic that directly executes machine instructions for maximum speed).
questions.explanationVi: Tại Level 1 (Control Level), bộ điều khiển vi chương trình (microprogrammed) dùng vi mã (microprogram) để dịch lệnh, còn bộ điều khiển kết dây (hardwired) dùng mạch phần cứng trực tiếp thực thi lệnh máy với tốc độ cao.

questions.concept: Steps of the Von Neumann Fetch-Decode-Execute Cycle
questions.question: In the Von Neumann architecture's fetch-decode-execute cycle, which register does the Control Unit use to determine the memory address of the next instruction to fetch?
options: Accumulator (AC)
Arithmetic-Logic Unit (ALU)
Program Counter (PC)
Status Flag Register
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.43 states: 'The control unit fetches the next instruction from memory, using the program counter to determine the location of that instruction.'
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 1.43, khối điều khiển (Control Unit) nạp lệnh kế tiếp từ bộ nhớ bằng cách sử dụng bộ đếm chương trình (Program Counter - PC) để xác định vị trí của lệnh đó.

questions.concept: Harvard Architecture vs. Von Neumann Architecture
questions.question: How does the Harvard architecture eliminate the instruction/data memory access bottleneck of the classic Von Neumann architecture?
options: By storing all instructions on magnetic tape and all data in CPU registers
By dividing memory into separate Program Memory and Data Memory, each with its own dedicated Address Bus and Data Bus
By eliminating the Control Unit and executing high-level C code directly in main memory
By replacing binary instructions with decimal floating-point numbers
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.47 explains that in Harvard architecture, memory is divided into Program memory and Data memory, and the CPU uses two separate system buses: an address/data bus pair for program memory and another address/data bus pair for data memory.
questions.explanationVi: Kiến trúc Harvard chia bộ nhớ thành Bộ nhớ chương trình (Program memory) và Bộ nhớ dữ liệu (Data memory) riêng biệt, đồng thời sử dụng 2 hệ thống bus (Address bus và Data bus) độc lập cho từng bộ nhớ.

questions.concept: First Generation Computers: ENIAC and IAS
questions.question: What was the major operational drawback of the ENIAC (1946) that prompted John von Neumann and his colleagues to design the IAS stored-program computer?
options: ENIAC used mechanical gears that jammed whenever performing division
ENIAC could only perform 5 additions per hour
ENIAC had to be programmed manually by setting switches and plugging/unplugging cables
ENIAC required liquid nitrogen cooling for its ULSI microprocessors
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.51 notes that although ENIAC could perform 5,000 additions per second using 18,000 vacuum tubes, its major drawback was that it had to be programmed manually by setting switches and plugging/unplugging cables.
questions.explanationVi: Nhược điểm lớn nhất của ENIAC (Slide 1.51) là phải lập trình thủ công bằng cách gạt công tắc và cắm/rút dây cáp, dẫn đến sự ra đời của máy tính chương trình lưu trữ (stored-program) IAS của von Neumann.

questions.concept: Moore's Law
questions.question: What trend did Gordon Moore observe regarding integrated circuits, and how did the pace adjust in the 1970s according to the lecture slides?
options: The clock frequency of vacuum tubes tripled every 6 months until 1990
The physical size of hard disk platters doubled every 24 months
The number of CPU registers in x86 processors doubled every 5 years
The number of transistors on a single chip was doubling every year initially, and slowed to doubling approximately every 18 months in the 1970s
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.57 states that Moore observed the number of transistors on a single chip was doubling every year, and the pace slowed to a doubling every 18 months in the 1970s, sustaining that rate for decades.
questions.explanationVi: Định luật Moore (Slide 1.57) phát biểu rằng số lượng transistor trên một chip tăng gấp đôi mỗi năm vào giai đoạn đầu, sau đó chậm lại ở mức tăng gấp đôi sau mỗi 18 tháng từ những năm 1970.

questions.subtopic: Intel Processor Evolution (4004 to Core i7)
questions.concept: Comparing Intel 1970s–2010s Processor Specifications
questions.question: According to the Evolution of Intel Processors tables (Slides 1.90–1.91), how did the Intel 8086 (1978) and Intel 8088 (1979) compare in bus width and addressable memory, and which processor first introduced a 32-bit bus width with 4 GB of addressable memory?
options: Both 8086 and 8088 had a 32-bit bus width; the 80286 (1982) introduced 4 GB addressable memory
Both 8086 and 8088 addressed 1 MB of memory, but 8086 had a 16-bit bus width while 8088 had an 8-bit bus width; the 386TM DX (1985) first introduced a 32-bit bus width and 4 GB addressable memory
The 8086 addressed 64 KB while the 8088 addressed 16 MB; the Pentium (1993) introduced 32-bit buses
The 4004 (1971) had an 8-bit bus width and 16 KB memory, while the 8080 had a 16-bit bus width
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.90 shows both 8086 and 8088 have 29,000 transistors and 1 MB addressable memory, but 8086 has a 16-bit bus width whereas 8088 has an 8-bit bus width. Slide 1.91 shows the 386TM DX (1985) introduced a 32-bit bus width, 4 GB addressable memory, and 64 TB virtual memory.
questions.explanationVi: Theo bảng Slide 1.90–1.91: cả 8086 và 8088 đều quản lý 1 MB bộ nhớ nhưng 8086 có bus 16-bit còn 8088 có bus 8-bit; bộ xử lý 386TM DX (1985) là chip đầu tiên có bus 32-bit và bộ nhớ định địa chỉ 4 GB.

questions.concept: 6-stage pipeline execution timing
questions.question: Consider the six-stage instruction pipeline (S1: Fetch instruction, S2: Decode opcode, S3: Calculate effective address, S4: Fetch operands, S5: Execute, S6: Store result) where each stage takes 1 clock cycle and stages overlap ideally with no stalls. How many total clock cycles are required to complete 10 sequential instructions, compared to a non-pipelined processor?
options: 60 clock cycles pipelined vs. 10 clock cycles non-pipelined
15 clock cycles pipelined vs. 60 clock cycles non-pipelined
16 clock cycles pipelined vs. 36 clock cycles non-pipelined
10 clock cycles pipelined vs. 60 clock cycles non-pipelined
questions.explanationEn: In a k-stage pipeline (with k = 6), the first instruction completes in k = 6 cycles, and each of the remaining (N - 1) = 9 instructions completes 1 cycle later: Total cycles = k + (N - 1) = 6 + (10 - 1) = 15 cycles. Without pipelining, 10 instructions × 6 cycles = 60 cycles.
questions.explanationVi: Trong pipeline k = 6 tầng lý tưởng, lệnh đầu tiên mất 6 chu kỳ, và 9 lệnh tiếp theo mỗi lệnh hoàn thành sau 1 chu kỳ tiếp theo: Tổng số chu kỳ = k + (N - 1) = 6 + 9 = 15 chu kỳ (so với 10 × 6 = 60 chu kỳ khi không có pipeline).
questions.stepByStep:
1. Number of stages k = 6; number of instructions N = 10.
2. Pipelined cycles = 6 + (10 - 1) = 15 clock cycles.
3. Non-pipelined cycles = 6 × 10 = 60 clock cycles.

questions.subtopic: Branch Prediction, Data Flow & Speculative Execution
questions.concept: Branch Prediction, Data Flow Analysis, and Speculative Execution
questions.question: Which microprocessor acceleration technique analyzes instruction dependencies on each other's data or results to create an optimized instruction schedule, working alongside branch prediction to enable speculative execution?
options: Fixed static branch trapping
Microcode ROM translation
Register window overlapping
Data flow analysis
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.67 defines Data flow analysis as: 'The processor analyzes which instructions are dependent on each other's results, or data, to create an optimized schedule of instructions.' Together with branch prediction, it enables speculative execution.
questions.explanationVi: Slide 1.67 định nghĩa Phân tích luồng dữ liệu (Data flow analysis) là kỹ thuật phân tích sự phụ thuộc dữ liệu/kết quả giữa các lệnh để tạo lịch thực thi tối ưu, kết hợp với dự đoán rẽ nhánh (branch prediction) để thực thi suy đoán (speculative execution).

questions.concept: Obstacles to increasing single-core clock speed & MIC
questions.question: According to Slides 1.94–1.95, what three physical issues limit further increases in single-processor clock speed, and what term describes chips integrating more than 50 cores?
options: Magnetic flux leakage, rotational latency, and seek time; Warehouse-Scale Cluster (WSC)
Segment overlap, page faults, and bus arbitration; Complex Instruction Set (CISC)
Heat dissipation (W/cm²), RC delay, and memory latency; Many Integrated Core (MIC)
Vacuum tube burnout, relay bounce, and punch-card jams; Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI)
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.94 lists the three obstacles to simply increasing clock rate: increased heat dissipation (W/cm²), RC delay, and memory latency. Slide 1.95 introduces the term Many Integrated Core (MIC) for chips with more than 50 cores.
questions.explanationVi: Slide 1.94 nêu 3 rào cản vật lý khi tăng xung nhịp: tản nhiệt (heat dissipation), trễ RC (RC delay), và độ trễ bộ nhớ (memory latency). Slide 1.95 giới thiệu thuật ngữ Many Integrated Core (MIC) cho các chip tích hợp trên 50 nhân.

questions.concept: Relative Performance Calculation
questions.question: A benchmark program takes 10 seconds to execute on Computer A and 15 seconds to execute on Computer B. What is the relative performance of Computer A compared to Computer B?
options: Computer B is 1.5 times faster than Computer A
Computer A is 0.67 times faster than Computer B
Computer A is 1.5 times faster than Computer B
Computer A is 5 times faster than Computer B
questions.explanationEn: Performance P = 1 / Execution Time. Therefore, P_A / P_B = t_B / t_A = 15s / 10s = 1.5. Computer A is 1.5 times faster than Computer B.
questions.explanationVi: Hiệu năng tỉ lệ nghịch với thời gian thực thi: P_A / P_B = t_B / t_A = 15s / 10s = 1.5. Vậy máy A nhanh gấp 1.5 lần máy B.
questions.stepByStep:
1. Identify execution times: t_A = 10 s, t_B = 15 s.
2. Apply relative performance formula: k = t_B / t_A = 15 / 10 = 1.5.
3. Conclude Computer A is 1.5 times faster than Computer B.

questions.concept: CPU Time and Target Clock Rate Tradeoff
questions.question: Computer A runs at a 2 GHz clock speed and executes a program in 10 seconds of CPU time. Engineers are designing Computer B to run the same program in 6 seconds of CPU time. A new hardware design allows a much higher clock rate, but increases the total number of clock cycles required by the program to 1.2 times that of Computer A. What clock rate must Computer B have?
options: 3.33 GHz
2.4 GHz
4.8 GHz
4.0 GHz
questions.explanationEn: First find Clock Cycles on Computer A: Cycles_A = CPU_Time_A × Clock_Rate_A = 10 s × (2 × 10^9 Hz) = 20 × 10^9 cycles. For Computer B, Cycles_B = 1.2 × Cycles_A = 24 × 10^9 cycles. To achieve CPU_Time_B = 6 s, Clock_Rate_B = Cycles_B / CPU_Time_B = (24 × 10^9) / 6 s = 4 × 10^9 Hz = 4.0 GHz.
questions.explanationVi: Số chu kỳ của máy A: Cycles_A = 10s × 2 GHz = 20 × 10^9 chu kỳ. Máy B cần Cycles_B = 1.2 × 20 × 10^9 = 24 × 10^9 chu kỳ. Để chạy trong 6s, tần số xung nhịp của máy B phải là: Clock_Rate_B = (24 × 10^9) / 6s = 4.0 GHz.
questions.formula: CPU Time = Clock Cycles / Clock Rate
questions.stepByStep:
1. Compute Clock Cycles for Computer A: Cycles_A = 10 s × 2 × 10^9 cycles/s = 20 × 10^9 cycles.
2. Compute Clock Cycles for Computer B: Cycles_B = 1.2 × (20 × 10^9) = 24 × 10^9 cycles.
3. Solve for Clock Rate of Computer B: Clock_Rate_B = (24 × 10^9 cycles) / 6 s = 4.0 × 10^9 Hz = 4.0 GHz.

questions.concept: Comparing two computers with the same ISA using CPI and Cycle Time
questions.question: Computer A has a clock cycle time of 250 ps and a CPI of 2.0 for a certain program. Computer B implements the exact same Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) and has a clock cycle time of 500 ps and a CPI of 1.2 for the same program. Which computer is faster, and by how much?
options: Computer A is 1.2 times faster than Computer B
Computer B is 1.2 times faster than Computer A
Computer A is 2.0 times faster than Computer B
Both computers execute the program in the exact same time
questions.explanationEn: Since both computers share the same ISA and run the same program, Instruction Count (IC) is identical. CPU_Time_A = IC × 2.0 × 250 ps = 500 × IC ps. CPU_Time_B = IC × 1.2 × 500 ps = 600 × IC ps. Therefore, P_A / P_B = CPU_Time_B / CPU_Time_A = 600 / 500 = 1.2.
questions.explanationVi: Vì cùng kiến trúc tập lệnh (ISA) nên số lệnh IC như nhau. Thời gian mỗi lệnh trung bình trên A là 2.0 × 250 ps = 500 ps; trên B là 1.2 × 500 ps = 600 ps. Do đó máy A nhanh hơn máy B là 600 / 500 = 1.2 lần.
questions.stepByStep:
1. Express CPU Time for Computer A: t_A = IC × 2.0 × 250 ps = 500·IC ps.
2. Express CPU Time for Computer B: t_B = IC × 1.2 × 500 ps = 600·IC ps.
3. Compute speedup ratio: t_B / t_A = (600·IC) / (500·IC) = 1.2 (Computer A is 1.2× faster).

questions.concept: Weighted Average CPI and Total Clock Cycles across Instruction Classes
questions.question: A processor has three instruction classes: Class A (CPI = 1), Class B (CPI = 2), and Class C (CPI = 3). A compiler generates Sequence 1 with instruction counts (A: 2, B: 1, C: 2) and Sequence 2 with instruction counts (A: 4, B: 1, C: 1). Which sequence executes in fewer total clock cycles, and what are the average CPIs of Sequence 1 and Sequence 2?
options: Sequence 1 is faster (5 clock cycles vs. 6 clock cycles); Avg CPI is 1.0 for Sequence 1 and 1.5 for Sequence 2
Sequence 1 and Sequence 2 tie at 10 clock cycles each; Avg CPI is 2.0 for both
Sequence 2 is faster (9 clock cycles vs. 10 clock cycles); Avg CPI is 2.0 for Sequence 1 and 1.5 for Sequence 2
Sequence 2 is faster (6 clock cycles vs. 10 clock cycles); Avg CPI is 1.5 for Sequence 1 and 2.0 for Sequence 2
questions.explanationEn: For Sequence 1: IC_1 = 2 + 1 + 2 = 5; Clock Cycles_1 = (2×1) + (1×2) + (2×3) = 10 cycles; Avg CPI_1 = 10 / 5 = 2.0. For Sequence 2: IC_2 = 4 + 1 + 1 = 6; Clock Cycles_2 = (4×1) + (1×2) + (1×3) = 9 cycles; Avg CPI_2 = 9 / 6 = 1.5. Even though Sequence 2 has more instructions (6 vs 5), it takes fewer total clock cycles (9 vs 10).
questions.explanationVi: Dãy 1: Tổng số lệnh IC = 5, Số chu kỳ = 2×1 + 1×2 + 2×3 = 10, CPI trung bình = 10/5 = 2.0. Dãy 2: Tổng số lệnh IC = 6, Số chu kỳ = 4×1 + 1×2 + 1×3 = 9, CPI trung bình = 9/6 = 1.5.
questions.formula: Clock Cycles = Sum(IC_i * CPI_i); Avg CPI = Clock Cycles / Total_IC
questions.stepByStep:
1. Sequence 1: IC = 2+1+2 = 5; Cycles = 2(1) + 1(2) + 2(3) = 10; Avg CPI = 10/5 = 2.0.
2. Sequence 2: IC = 4+1+1 = 6; Cycles = 4(1) + 1(2) + 1(3) = 9; Avg CPI = 9/6 = 1.5.
3. Compare total cycles: 9 < 10, so Sequence 2 executes in fewer cycles.

questions.concept: Calculating MIPS and understanding its limitations
questions.question: A processor runs at a clock rate of 3.2 GHz and executes a program with an average CPI of 1.6. What is its MIPS (Millions of Instructions Per Second) rating for this program, and why can MIPS be misleading when comparing two different computers?
options: 2,000 MIPS; because MIPS does not account for differences in ISAs or instruction complexity between computers
5,120 MIPS; because MIPS only measures hard disk rotational latency
200 MIPS; because MIPS assumes every instruction takes 100 clock cycles
1,600 MIPS; because MIPS is only valid for mechanical calculating machines
questions.explanationEn: Using the formula on Slide 1.81: MIPS = Clock Rate / (CPI × 10^6) = (3.2 × 10^9) / (1.6 × 10^6) = 2,000 MIPS. Slide 1.81 notes that MIPS fails to account for differences in ISAs and instruction complexity across machines.
questions.explanationVi: Áp dụng công thức Slide 1.81: MIPS = Clock Rate / (CPI × 10^6) = (3.2 × 10^9) / (1.6 × 10^6) = 2000 MIPS. Chỉ số MIPS có hạn chế vì không tính đến sự khác biệt về tập lệnh (ISA) và độ phức tạp của từng lệnh giữa các máy khác nhau.

questions.subtopic: CISC vs. RISC Characteristics & Cycle Comparison
questions.concept: CISC vs. RISC Multiplication Program Fragment Cycle Comparison
questions.question: On Slide 1.100, multiplying 10 by 5 is implemented in CISC using two `mov` instructions (1 cycle each) and one `mul` instruction (30 cycles), whereas in RISC it is implemented using a loop with 3 `mov` instructions (1 cycle each), 5 `add` instructions (1 cycle each), and 5 `loop` branches (1 cycle each). How many total clock cycles does each version require?
options: CISC version: 3 clock cycles; RISC version: 13 clock cycles
CISC version: 32 clock cycles; RISC version: 13 clock cycles
CISC version: 32 clock cycles; RISC version: 30 clock cycles
CISC version: 15 clock cycles; RISC version: 25 clock cycles
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.100 calculates: CISC cycles = (2 movs × 1 cycle) + (1 mul × 30 cycles) = 32 clock cycles. RISC cycles = (3 movs × 1 cycle) + (5 adds × 1 cycle) + (5 loops × 1 cycle) = 13 clock cycles.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 1.100: Phiên bản CISC cần (2 lệnh mov × 1 chu kỳ) + (1 lệnh mul × 30 chu kỳ) = 32 chu kỳ. Phiên bản RISC cần (3 lệnh mov × 1) + (5 lệnh add × 1) + (5 lệnh loop × 1) = 13 chu kỳ.

questions.concept: RISC Overlapping Register Windows and CWP
questions.question: How do RISC architectures use overlapping register windows and the Current Window Pointer (CWP) to reduce procedure-call overhead?
options: They copy the entire main memory stack into the L1 instruction cache on every jump instruction

Instead of pushing/popping parameters on a memory stack, the Outputs register subset of the calling procedure overlaps with the Inputs register subset of the called procedure, and CWP shifts to point to the active window
They use microcode ROM tables to translate 8-bit registers into 64-bit virtual addresses
They disable all CPU registers during subroutine execution and access operands directly from disk
questions.explanationEn: Slides 1.101–1.102 explain that RISC machines use a large register file divided into Globals and overlapping windows (Inputs, Locals, Outputs). When Procedure One calls Procedure Two, Procedure One's Output registers become Procedure Two's Input registers, and the Current Window Pointer (CWP) updates to point to the active register window.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 1.101–1.102, kiến trúc RISC sử dụng các cửa sổ thanh ghi chồng lấp (Overlapping Register Windows). Các thanh ghi Output của thủ tục gọi trùng với thanh ghi Input của thủ tục được gọi, và con trỏ CWP (Current Window Pointer) trỏ tới cửa sổ thanh ghi đang hoạt động giúp truyền tham số không cần qua stack bộ nhớ.

options: SISD for vector processors; MISD for modern multicore systems
SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) for vector processors; MIMD (Multiple Instruction, Multiple Data) for modern parallel multicore systems
MIMD for classic uniprocessors; SIMD for single-core microcontrollers
MISD for vector processors; SISD for warehouse-scale clusters
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.104 defines SISD as classic uniprocessors, SIMD as executing the same instruction on multiple data values (as in vector processors), MIMD as multiple instruction streams on multiple data streams (today's parallel architectures), and MISD as multiple instruction streams on a single data stream.
questions.explanationVi: Theo phân loại Flynn (Slide 1.104): SISD là máy đơn bộ xử lý cổ điển; SIMD thực thi cùng một lệnh trên nhiều luồng dữ liệu (như bộ xử lý vector/GPU); MIMD thực thi nhiều luồng lệnh trên nhiều luồng dữ liệu (các kiến trúc song song đa nhân hiện đại).

questions.concept: Amdahl's Law speedup calculation (f=80%, k=2x)
questions.question: A program spends 80% of its execution time in a computational module that is enhanced to run 2x faster (k = 2.0), while the remaining 20% of execution time is unaffected. According to Amdahl's Law, what is the overall system speedup S (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.explanationVi: Áp dụng định luật Amdahl: S = 1 / ((1 - 0.8) + (0.8 / 2.0)) = 1.67.
questions.stepByStep:
1. Identify fraction enhanced f = 0.8 and component speedup k = 2.0.
2. Compute new normalized time = (1 - 0.8) + (0.8 / 2.0) = 0.6000.
3. Compute reciprocal S = 1 / 0.6000 ≈ 1.67.

questions.concept: Weighted Average CPI calculation (50 instructions)
questions.question: A program executes 50 instructions divided into three classes: Class A (10 instructions, CPI = 1), Class B (20 instructions, CPI = 2), and Class C (20 instructions, CPI = 3). What are the total clock cycles required and the weighted average CPI?
options: 110 clock cycles; Average CPI = 2.20
130 clock cycles; Average CPI = 2.60
100 clock cycles; Average CPI = 2.00
95 clock cycles; Average CPI = 1.90
questions.explanationEn: Total Clock Cycles = (10×1) + (20×2) + (20×3) = 110 cycles. Weighted Average CPI = 110 / 50 = 2.20.
questions.explanationVi: Tổng số chu kỳ xung nhịp = (10×1) + (20×2) + (20×3) = 110 chu kỳ. CPI trung bình = 110 / 50 = 2.20.
questions.formula: Clock Cycles = Sum(IC_i * CPI_i); CPI = Clock Cycles / Total_IC
questions.stepByStep:
1. Sum instruction counts: Total IC = 10 + 20 + 20 = 50.
2. Compute weighted clock cycles: 10(1) + 20(2) + 20(3) = 110 cycles.
3. Divide by Total IC: CPI = 110 / 50 = 2.20.

questions.concept: Role of Compiler vs. Operating System in System Software

Compiler (translates high-level code into machine code) and Operating System (handles scheduling, resource allocation, memory/storage management, and I/O control)

questions.explanationVi: Slide 1.34 nêu rõ 2 thành phần chính của Phần mềm hệ thống (System Software): Trình biên dịch (Compiler - dịch mã bậc cao sang mã máy) và Hệ điều hành (OS - lập lịch, cấp phát tài nguyên, quản lý bộ nhớ/lưu trữ và điều khiển I/O).

questions.concept: Real-world pipeline depths in Pentium, Pentium IV, and Itanium
questions.question: According to Slide 1.65 on real-world examples of instruction-level pipelining, how many pipeline stages did the original Intel Pentium, the Pentium IV, and the Itanium (IA-64) processors have?
options: First Pentium: 10-stage pipeline; Pentium IV: 5-stage pipeline; Itanium: 24-stage pipeline
First Pentium: 6-stage pipeline; Pentium IV: 12-stage pipeline; Itanium: 32-stage pipeline
First Pentium: two 5-stage pipelines; Pentium IV: 24-stage pipeline; Itanium (IA-64): 10-stage pipeline
All three processors used an identical 6-stage pipeline

questions.subtopic: Branch Prediction, Data Flow & Speculative Execution
questions.concept: Four types of branch prediction
questions.question: In Slide 1.66, how is 'Dynamic branch prediction' distinguished from 'Fixed', 'True', and 'Static' branch predictions?
options: Dynamic prediction never changes over time and always predicts the branch is never taken
Dynamic prediction is performed exclusively by the compiler before the program runs
Dynamic prediction uses historical runtime information about the branch and its past outcomes, whereas Static prediction does not use any execution history
Dynamic prediction requires halting the processor pipeline until the branch target is manually entered
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.66 lists four ways predictions are made: Fixed predictions do not change over time; True predictions result in the branch being always taken or never taken; Dynamic prediction uses historical information about the branch and its outcomes; Static prediction does not use any history.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 1.66, dự đoán rẽ nhánh động (Dynamic prediction) sử dụng thông tin lịch sử thực thi của lệnh rẽ nhánh và kết quả trước đó, trong khi dự đoán tĩnh (Static prediction) không sử dụng lịch sử thực thi.

questions.concept: CPU Execution Time from IC, CPI, and Clock Rate
questions.question: A program consists of 4.5 × 10^9 instructions and executes on a processor running at 3.0 GHz with an average CPI of 1.5. What is the CPU execution time (t_CPU) of this program?
options: 1.50 seconds
3.00 seconds
2.25 seconds
1.00 second
questions.explanationVi: Áp dụng công thức Slide 1.80: t_CPU = (IC × CPI) / f_0 = (4.5 × 10^9 × 1.5) / (3.0 × 10^9) = 2.25 giây.
questions.stepByStep:
1. Multiply IC by CPI: Total Clock Cycles = 4.5 × 10^9 × 1.5 = 6.75 × 10^9 cycles.
2. Divide by Clock Rate f_0 = 3.0 × 10^9 Hz: t_CPU = 6.75 / 3.0 = 2.25 seconds.

questions.subtopic: CISC vs. RISC Characteristics & Cycle Comparison
questions.concept: CISC vs. RISC performance equation strategy
questions.question: In terms of the basic computer performance equation (CPU Time = Instructions/Program × Avg Cycles/Instruction × Seconds/Cycle), how do RISC and CISC systems fundamentally differ in their optimization strategy?
options: RISC systems reduce the number of instructions per program using complex microcoded instructions, whereas CISC systems only access memory via explicit load/store instructions

RISC systems shorten execution time primarily by reducing the average clock cycles per instruction (CPI) using fixed-length instructions and hardwired control, whereas CISC systems aim to reduce the number of instructions per program
Both RISC and CISC require microcode interpreters for every arithmetic instruction
CISC uses fixed-length instructions to simplify pipelining, whereas RISC uses variable-length instructions
questions.explanationEn: Slides 1.97–1.99 state that RISC systems shorten execution time by reducing clock cycles per instruction (using fixed-length instructions, load/store memory access, and hardwired control), whereas CISC systems aim to reduce the number of instructions per program.
questions.explanationVi: Theo Slide 1.98–1.99: Hệ thống RISC rút ngắn thời gian thực thi bằng cách giảm số chu kỳ trên mỗi lệnh (CPI) nhờ lệnh có độ dài cố định và bộ điều khiển kết dây (hardwired), trong khi CISC tìm cách giảm tổng số lệnh của chương trình.

questions.subtopic: Intel Processor Evolution (4004 to Core i7)
questions.concept: Comparing Pentium III, Pentium 4, Core 2 Duo, and Core i7 EE 4960X
questions.question: According to the 'Recent Processors' table on Slide 1.93 (Pentium III, Pentium 4, Core 2 Duo, Core i7 EE 4960X), how did feature size, transistor count, and core count evolve from the Pentium 4 (2000) to the Core i7 EE 4960X (2013)?
options: Feature size grew from 22 nm to 250 nm, transistor count stayed at 42 million, and core count increased from 2 to 64
Feature size shrank from 65 nm to 10 nm, transistor count grew from 9.5 million to 167 million, and core count increased from 1 to 2
Feature size shrank from 180 nm to 22 nm, transistor count grew from 42 million to 1.86 billion, and number of cores increased from 1 to 6
All four processors had 64 GB addressable memory and 8 cores
questions.explanationEn: Slide 1.93 shows Pentium 4 (2000) had 180 nm feature size, 42 million transistors, and 1 core; Core 2 Duo (2006) had 65 nm, 167 million transistors, and 2 cores; Core i7 EE 4960X (2013) had 22 nm feature size, 1.86 billion transistors, and 6 cores.
questions.explanationVi: Theo bảng Slide 1.93: từ Pentium 4 (2000) đến Core i7 EE 4960X (2013), kích thước transistor thu nhỏ từ 180 nm xuống 22 nm, số lượng transistor tăng từ 42 triệu lên 1.86 tỷ, và số nhân (cores) tăng từ 1 lên 6.
